target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Mystery of the Treasure Map
lecture_lines: Meet Vector-Bot, searching for hidden treasure.
Two paths define the treasure's exact location.
We represent this system as Ax equals b.
animations: Fade in Vector-Bot [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg] at the origin (0,0) and a treasure chest icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treasure.svg] at (1,2) in the coordinate system.
Draw two lines: 2x + y = 4 (#1E90FF) and x + 2y = 5 (#FFA500) that intersect precisely at the treasure chest [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/treasure.svg] location.
Transform the system of lines into the matrix notation Ax = b (#FFFFFF) positioned in the upper right corner.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Determinant as Area
lecture_lines: Determinants represent the signed area in 2D.
Column vectors v1 and v2 form a parallelogram.
Let's visualize this area on the coordinate grid.
Calculations show the area equals the determinant.
This area is our fundamental scaling factor.
animations: Draw vectors v1=(2,1) in #FFFF00 and v2=(1,2) in #00FF00 starting from the origin.
Draw the two missing sides to complete the parallelogram formed by v1 and v2.
Fill the interior of the parallelogram with #33CCFF at 0.3 opacity to represent the area.
Pulse the parallelogram scaling and label it 'Area = det(A)' using #FFFFFF.
Write the determinant calculation '2*2 - 1*1 = 3' in #FFFFFF at the bottom of the screen.

sections.title: The Geometric Setup of Ax = b
lecture_lines: Ax equals b scales our basis vectors.
We stretch v1 by x and v2 by y.
Their sum reaches the target vector b.
animations: Draw the target vector b=(4,5) in #FF00FF starting from the origin on the existing grid.
Animate the scaling of v1 by x and v2 by y, then add them tip-to-tail to reach vector b.
Fade in labels 'x*v1' and 'y*v2' in #FFFFFF next to the respective scaled segments.

sections.title: The 'Shear' Insight for x
lecture_lines: To find x, consider the area (b, v2).
Substitute b with x v1 plus y v2.
The y v2 component is parallel to v2.
Shearing along v2 does not change the area.
This leaves only the area of x v1.
animations: Construct a new parallelogram using vector b (#FF00FF) as one side and v2 (#00FF00) as the base.
Visually decompose b into its components x*v1 and y*v2.
Animate a shear transformation that slides the top side of the parallelogram from b to x*v1.
Highlight that the 'y*v2' component, being parallel to the base v2, does not change the area.
Display the equation 'Area(b, v2) = x * Area(v1, v2)' in #FFFFFF at the top.

sections.title: Deriving the Ratio (Cramer's Formula)
lecture_lines: Area(b, v2) equals x times Area(v1, v2).
Solving for x gives a ratio of areas.
This is the determinant Ab over det A.
Ab replaces the first column with vector b.
We have geometrically derived Cramer's Rule!
animations: Display the parallelogram (b, v2) and (v1, v2) side-by-side or stacked to show their comparison.
Create a fraction bar and place 'Area(b, v2)' in the numerator and 'Area(v1, v2)' in the denominator.
Transform the area labels into the determinant notation: 'det([b, v2]) / det([v1, v2])'.
Substitute the example values to show '3 / 3 = 1' and highlight 'x = 1' in #FFFFFF.
Flash the result 'x = 1' to emphasize the successful derivation of the first variable.

sections.title: Scaling to y and Summary
lecture_lines: Apply the same logic to solve for y.
Swap the second column with target vector b.
Cramer's Rule turns algebra into geometric ratios.
animations: Briefly show the parallelogram (v1, b) and its ratio to (v1, v2) to solve for y.
Display 'y = 2' and animate Vector-Bot moving to the coordinates (1, 2) on the grid.
Fade in the general Cramer's Rule formula 'xi = det(Ai) / det(A)' in #FFFFFF for the summary.
